description: Search ALL leads the account has ever collected (across every search) with filters and sorting — no new search is run and no leads are spent. A Google listing found more than once appears once, with its most recent data. Up to 1,000 leads per call (default 25). When next_cursor is set, call again with cursor = next_cursor for the next page: the cursor carries its filters and sort, so it can be sent alone. Pass search_id to query one search's leads instead of the whole library. Example — plumbers in Austin rated 4.5 or higher with a safe email, most-reviewed first: filters=[{field:'category',operator:'contains',value:'plumb'},{field:'city',operator:'is',value:'Austin',conj:'and'},{field:'rating',operator:'gte',value:'4.5',conj:'and'},{field:'email_status',operator:'is',value:'safe',conj:'and'}], sort=[{id:'reviews',dir:-1}]. A field, operator or value the tool cannot use comes back as an error that names it and lists what works.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous call, for the next page. It carries that call's filters and sort: send it alone, or with the same filters and sort — different ones are refused. Leave it out to start a new query.

filters.description: Conditions, each {field, operator, value, conj}; omit to match every lead. text fields [operators: contains, not_contains, is, is_not, is_empty, is_not_empty]: name, category, city, state, address, website, primary_email (or email_1), email_2, email_3, primary_phone (or phone_1), phone_carrier (or phone_1_carrier), phone_2, phone_2_carrier, phone_3, phone_3_carrier, owner_name, social_facebook, social_instagram, social_linkedin, social_x, social_youtube, social_tiktok, social_yelp, gbp_url, google_cid, logo_url, main_image_url. number fields [operators: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, is_empty, is_not_empty]: rank, rating, reviews. yes/no fields [operators: is_true, is_false, is_empty, is_not_empty]: claimed. choice fields [operators: is, is_not, is_empty, is_not_empty]: email_status (or email_1_status), email_2_status, email_3_status take safe, risky, invalid, unknown; phone_line_type (or phone_1_type), phone_2_type, phone_3_type take mobile, fixed_line (Landline), fixed_line_or_mobile (Landline or mobile), voip, non_fixed_voip, toll_free (Toll-free), premium_rate, shared_cost, personal_number (Personal), pager, uan, voicemail, unknown. value is one string (a number as text, e.g. '4.5'); is_empty, is_not_empty, is_true and is_false take none. Text matching ignores case. Phone fields compare digits, so '(512) 555' finds +15125550100; website is / is_not compare domains when given a domain ('acme.com', or 'https://www.acme.com/'), and whole addresses when given a path, a query or a fragment ('acme.com/locations/austin'), either way ignoring http(s)://, www. and a closing slash. conj ('and' or 'or') joins a condition to the one before it, and 'and' binds tighter: A and B or C means (A and B) or C. To match any of several values, send one condition per value joined with conj 'or', repeating the other conditions in each group.

search_id.description: Only this search's leads (a search_id from search_leads or list_searches) — e.g. to narrow one search before export_leads with the same search_id and filters. Omit to query the whole library.

sort.description: Sort keys in priority order, e.g. [{id:'reviews',dir:-1}] for most-reviewed first. id is any filter field id (the column ids email_1, email_1_status, phone_1, phone_1_type and phone_1_carrier work too); dir is 1 ascending (the default) or -1 descending. A lead with no value for a key (null) sorts after the leads that have one, in either direction — except social_facebook, social_instagram, social_linkedin, social_x, social_youtube, social_tiktok, social_yelp, gbp_url, logo_url, main_image_url, which sort by whether a lead has one, not by the link: ascending puts the leads WITHOUT one first, so use dir -1 to put the leads that have one first. Without a sort the order is arbitrary but stable.

name: query_leads

data_sources.description: Where the sources, licences and notices are for emails and owner names that may come from open datasets and public records. Pass it on with any of this data you share.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as 'cursor' for the next page (it carries the filters and sort); null on the last page.

address.description: Street address from the Google listing.

claimed.description: Whether the owner has claimed the Google listing.

email_status.description: Email 1's SMTP verdict: safe | risky | invalid | unknown.

google_cid.description: Google listing id (the query_leads google_cid field).

maps_url.description: The Google Maps link for the listing.

phone_line_type.description: Phone 1's line type: mobile, fixed_line, voip or toll_free usually; also unknown, fixed_line_or_mobile and the other values query_leads lists.

phones_data.description: Verified phones with line type + carrier.

primary_email.description: Email 1: the first address in emails_data, the one email_status describes. Before emails are verified, the lead's primary address.

primary_phone.description: Phone 1: the first number in phones_data, the one phone_line_type describes. Before phones are verified, the lead's primary number, or its Google Maps number.

socials.description: Social profile links keyed by platform.

total_matching.description: Exact match count — on the first page only; null on later pages.

title: Query the lead library
